Fundamental — what it's worth: Built up from the automotive business, energy generation & storage, services, net cash, and a probability-weighted autonomy option — what is it worth?
Five independent valuation methods, blended into one weighted central fair value; the autonomy-at-scale case carries a full quarter of the weight.

The sum-of-the-parts spans a wide range — the operating businesses at ~$127, an autonomy option risk-weighted to reach ~$230 (base), up to ~$560 if the option is credited at full scale. The autonomy option is the swing factor. Full detail and the five lenses are in the study and the open model.
Technical & price structure: In plain terms: Tesla trades far above our weighted central fair value — richly valued on the operating businesses, with almost the entire premium resting on the autonomy bet. It is best read as an operating company — a profitable EV maker, a fast-growing energy-storage business, and a small services arm — wrapped around a large option on autonomy and robotics (Full Self-Driving, Robotaxi and Optimus) whose cash flows do not yet exist. On operating cash flows and earnings the business is worth roughly USD 90–230 a share; the bull case (~$560, the top of the sum-of-the-parts) needs Robotaxi and Optimus to scale into large, high-margin businesses, while the cautious case (~$103) is autonomy stalling as the multiple de-rates. What moves it is how likely, how large and how soon the autonomy businesses become real — an outcome the market observes only through the price.
Monte Carlo — where could the price go?: 50,000 paths, 16 forces: FSD/Robotaxi monetization, delivery volumes, auto ASP/margin, energy-storage growth, Nasdaq/high-beta flows, US real rates and input costs/FX — plus event forces: a Robotaxi/unsupervised-FSD milestone, a quarterly delivery print, a quarterly earnings/margin print, Optimus progress, a China demand/price-war shock, an EV-credit/tariff/FSD-probe policy event, a key-person/governance event, a broad Nasdaq risk-off, and an energy megadeal. Details in the methodology .
Peer set & risks: Tesla competes across several arenas — EVs, energy storage, autonomy software, robotaxis, humanoid robots and charging — and its position differs sharply in each. Rivals trade in different currencies and aren't directly value-comparable, so this is a competitive map, not a price table.
The investment debate turns less on any single arena than on the autonomy option — how much of the price the unproven Robotaxi, FSD and Optimus businesses justify. Competitive map, not advice.

How is the Tesla valuation calculated? — The study triangulates five lenses — a segment sum-of-the-parts (the automotive business, energy generation and storage, services, net cash, and a probability-weighted autonomy option); a consolidated discounted cash flow; a relative-multiples cross-check; a through-cycle normalized-earnings view; and, given explicit weight, the autonomy-at-scale case in which the option is credited close to full value — then expresses the result as a 50,000-path Monte Carlo probability distribution. Every assumption is visible and editable in the free Excel model.

Does testahil recommend buying or selling Tesla? — No. testahil never issues buy, sell, or hold recommendations. It publishes fair-value ranges and probability distributions as educational material, and grades its own forecasts publicly when they resolve.
